cross_field_relationships.description: White dwarf cooling timescales are fundamentally governed by mass-dependent radius and heat capacity. Increased mass leads to higher central density and smaller radius (via electron degeneracy pressure), reducing the total thermal energy reservoir and accelerating initial photon diffusion cooling. Additionally, core crystallization onset and latent heat release scale with mass, making cooling age a strict functional dependency of mass and effective temperature in stellar evolution models.

Surface gravity (g = GM/R²) is directly determined by the mass-radius relation of degenerate matter. For white dwarfs, greater mass compresses the star further (R ∝ M⁻¹/³ in the non-relativistic limit, steepening near the Chandrasekhar limit), causing log g to increase monotonically with mass. This is a strict consequence of hydrostatic equilibrium balanced by relativistic/non-relativistic electron degeneracy pressure.

These fields are not directly linked by a fundamental physical law but exhibit statistical correlation within theoretical cooling model grids and observational parameter spaces. Cooling age traces thermal evolution along an isomass track (primarily mapping to Teff), while log g defines the structural track itself. They represent independent physical degrees of freedom (thermal history vs. compactness) but are often observationally coupled due to degeneracies in spectroscopic atmospheric fitting, instrumental resolution limits, and model grid interpolation assumptions.

suitable_use_cases: Reference benchmark for high-mass white dwarf structural parameters (M ≈ 1.0 M☉, log g ≈ 8.6)

Testing general relativity via gravitational redshift measurements in tight binaries
Calibrating spectroscopic atmospheric fitting pipelines for DA white dwarfs
Stellar evolution timeline reconstruction (progenitor MS lifetime + WD cooling age)
limitations: Highly object-specific (Sirius B only); not representative of WD population statistics or IMF
Significant literature coverage gaps: multiple key references lack mass, cooling_age, or surface_gravity values
Mass estimates contain extreme outliers (>1.4 M☉) that violate the Chandrasekhar limit and require strict filtering
Cooling age derivation relies entirely on theoretical interpolation grids; uncertainties depend heavily on assumed core composition (C/O ratio) and envelope thickness
Unit inconsistency in cooling_age (Myr vs. Gyr) requires careful conversion before cross-dataset merging
recommended_caveats: Exclude any mass values >1.4 M☉ as likely typographical, progenitor confusion, or methodological artifacts
Apply unit normalization (convert all cooling ages to Gyr) and verify source methodology before aggregation
Treat cooling_age and surface_gravity as observationally coupled but physically independent; avoid assuming direct causal scaling without model context
When using for population studies, supplement with larger survey catalogs (e.g., SDSS DR12, Gaia EDR3) to address coverage gaps
Acknowledge model dependency: reported values reflect specific cooling/atmosphere grid assumptions (e.g., BaSTI, MESA variants); cite corresponding model versions
